> A desk buddy with a 1.3" animated TFT face on a custom ESP32-S3 PCB. Three servos let it turn, nod and tilt its head, so the face can look around and react. A push button on the base wakes it up and changes its mood. The case is 3D printed with tolerances tuned for FDM.

Designed the electronics and case for DeskBuddy, a desk robot with a 1.3" ST7789 SPI screen as its face and three MG90S servos that let it turn, nod and tilt its head.

Electronics (KiCad): Drew the schematic around an ESP32-S3-Zero, with the screen on SPI, a push button, and the servos on a separate 5V rail with a 1000 µF cap and a screw terminal. I routed the PCB and checked the wiring against the screen pinout. When the 3D models showed up missing, I fixed the KiCad library paths and exported a full STEP of the board.

Case (Fusion 360): I first tried getting AI to make the case, but it was bad. The head couldn’t move properly and it had no face. So I redesigned it myself, which took ages. It now has a base that holds the PCB, a lid with the pan servo, a neck with a nod servo, and a head pod with a tilt servo. The face plate has a window for the screen, and there’s a button plunger through the lid. I imported the real servo and screen models to check fit and collisions across the full range of movement, and set the tolerances for FDM printing.

Still to do: The case works mechanically but looks very boxy and plain, so I want to change the looks, with rounded edges, a friendlier head shape and nicer proportions. After that I’ll write the firmware for the three servos and the animated face, print the parts, and order the PCB.
